title: Parametric Social Identity Injection and Diversification in Public Opinion Simulation

problem.claim: LLM-based public opinion simulation methods fail to capture social diversity, producing flattened inter-group differences and overly homogeneous demographic-group responses.

gap.claim: Existing simulation methods do not adequately preserve distinct social identities in LLM representations.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Parametric Social Identity Injection, a framework that injects explicit parametric demographic attributes and value orientations into intermediate LLM hidden states.
The framework provides fine-grained, controllable identity modulation at the representation level rather than through prompt-based persona conditioning.
The paper identifies Diversity Collapse as a phenomenon in which distinct social identities become increasingly indistinguishable across LLM layers.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish PSII from prompt-based persona conditioning by introducing representation-level identity modulation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on the World Values Survey using multiple open-source LLMs reportedly show improved distributional fidelity and diversity with PSII.
The authors report reduced KL divergence to real-world survey data and enhanced overall diversity.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are being adopted as scalable alternatives to costly and slow human surveys for public opinion simulation.
Current LLM-based methods produce insufficient social diversity and homogeneous demographic-group responses.
The limitation is characterized as Diversity Collapse in LLM hidden representations.
PSII injects explicit parametric social identity information into intermediate hidden states and enables controllable representation-level modulation.
Experiments on World Values Survey data reportedly improve fidelity and diversity across multiple open-source LLMs.

source_observation.claim: Social identities may become less distinguishable across layers in LLM-based simulation representations.

interpretation.claim: Representation-level controls may address identity homogenization more directly than prompt-only conditioning.

application.claim: For demographic simulation, explicitly parameterized identity attributes and value orientations could be injected into intermediate representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported survey setting or models.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the open-source LLMs, dataset configuration, evaluation protocol, or statistical significance details.
The abstract does not describe the PSII architecture, training procedure, computational cost, or failure cases.
